fact: The Mauritius Standards Bureau Act establishes the Mauritius Standards Bureau and a Standards Council, and the Minister made the Certification Mark Regulations 2026 (GN No. 46 of 2026) under section 33 of that Act on the Council's recommendation.

The MSB register of its National Information Security Management System Certification Scheme lists certificates against MS ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the Mauritian-standard designation of the information security standard.

The Mauritius Standards Bureau certifies organisations under its National ISMS Certification Scheme; its register as at 31 December 2025 lists ten certificates against MS ISO/IEC 27001:2022, all marked as accredited, issued by the MSB (certifier: Mauritius Standards Bureau).

The MSB register lists certificates against MS ISO/IEC 27001:2022 held by the Passport and Immigration Office, CERT-MU, the Mauritius Revenue Authority, the Central Information Systems Division of the ICT ministry, the Police IT Unit and the National Sanctions Secretariat, all valid at 31 December 2025, with certificates issued 2025 (certifier: Mauritius Standards Bureau).

Emtel states its data centre was first certified by the Mauritius Standards Bureau against MS ISO/IEC 27001 in 2013 and upgraded to the 2013 version in 2015 (certifier: Mauritius Standards Bureau); the document carries no date of its own and its published date, 2019-11-26, is derived from its posting path, so the event dates are 2013 and 2015.

The Energy Efficiency (Refrigerating Appliances) Regulations 2026, in operation from 1 May 2026, name the Mauritius Standards Bureau as a body established under the Mauritius Standards Bureau Act, which the regulations use to verify appliance compliance with the energy performance standards; the document names no IT or data standard.

The Mauritius Standards Bureau annual report 2021/2022 states the Bureau became a corporate body under the Mauritius Standards Bureau Act 1993, in effect from 16 July 1993, with the object of preparing, framing, amending and revising standards, and developing Mauritian Standards (MS).

The Bureau's own Quality Assurance Unit, as third-party certification body, ran the National Information Security Management System Certification Scheme (ISO/IEC 27001) under its National Management Systems Certification Scheme Regulations 2008, and in 2021/2022 maintained certification of eight organisations to ISO/IEC 27001; the report names none of the eight, and says the scheme is accredited by MAURITAS for information security management systems.
system: National Information Security Management System Certification Scheme
